config.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding

personas.name: Joyce
personas.role: Mother of the bride, keeps the family organized
personas.hidden_agenda: Worried the Lagos relatives will feel second-class

personas.name: Amara
personas.goals: A relaxed wedding where her family and Theo's mix well
personas.hidden_agenda: Already decided on her readings and is waiting to be asked

personas.name: Tobi
personas.role: Cousin, handling travel for the out-of-town guests
personas.goals: Get everyone from the airport to the hotel
personas.hidden_agenda: Hasn't booked the airport van yet

personas.name: Ingrid
personas.role: Theo's grandmother, joining to help with the reception
personas.goals: Make the Swedish side feel part of it
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to bake a traditional cake

pack.title: Amara and Theo's wedding - Sunday family call

agenda.title: Who's doing what
agenda.goal: Give every open job a name

beats.summary: Time and readings; Ingrid misremembers the date, gently corrected
Venue, caterer and cake; Joyce misremembers the deposit; the cake question
The Lagos guests, hotel rooms and the airport; Tobi's hotel rate is off and stays off
Who's doing what; one job gets an owner, one doesn't

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Hello, my dear, can you hear us all right, Ingrid?

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Oh, lovely, yes, I can hear you. Theo set it up for me.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Wonderful. So, the ceremony first. Amara, the time is still half past two?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Half two, yes. The church needed the morning for a christening.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: And that's on the twenty-eighth, isn't it? I have it on my calendar.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: It's the twenty-first, Ingrid. June twenty-first.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: The twenty-first. Oh dear, my calendar is wrong, then. In my day we just remembered.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Basically, the twenty-first is when the Lagos flights land the day before, so it's good.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: How many can the church hold, again?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: A hundred and twenty. We're well under that.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: And the readings, my dear? Have you chosen?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Honestly, I was hoping someone would ask. I'd like Auntie Bisi to read one, and Ingrid to read the other.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Oh, lovely. In Swedish, or English?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Whichever you prefer. Theo said Swedish would make his dad cry.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Then Swedish. I'd be honoured.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Who walks you in, then? Your father, of course.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Dad and you, Mum. Both of you. If that's okay.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Oh, my dear. Of course it's okay.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Basically, there won't be a dry eye in the place.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: So, Bisi and Ingrid for the readings, and both parents walk Amara in. That's settled, then.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Settled. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Let me see, the reception. The hall is booked, and the caterer has the deposit. We paid them two thousand, I think.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: It was twelve hundred, Mum. The rest is due a month before.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Twelve hundred. Yes. I was thinking of the hall.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: The hall was sixty-eight hundred, right?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Sixty-eight hundred. Theo's parents are covering half of that.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: About the cake. I wondered whether I might bake a prinsesstårta, for the Swedish side.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Oh, Ingrid, that would be amazing.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: But we have the three-tier cake ordered already.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Mine would be small. Just a little one, next to it.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Two cakes is basically the dream.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Maybe we could have both. Let me think about where it would go.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Honestly, Mum, there's room. The dessert table is huge.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Then yes. The three-tier cake, and Ingrid's cake next to it. Both.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Oh, lovely. I'll bake it the morning before and bring it in a tin.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Is the caterer okay with outside food, though? Some of them are funny about it.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Let me see, the menu. Jollof and the Swedish meatballs both, yes?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Both. Theo's brother says it's the best idea anyone's had.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: In my day, the meatballs were the whole menu.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Did Theo ever finish building that canoe, by the way?

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Oh, the canoe. It's in my garage. It has been in my garage for three years.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: It leaks. He won't admit it, but it leaks.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Okay, okay. Back to the wedding.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Travel. Tobi, you're our travel person.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: No wahala. So, nine guests are flying in from Lagos.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Nine. And the hotel?

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: We're holding eighteen rooms, at a hundred and nine a night. Not bad.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: That's good. Is breakfast included?

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Basically, yes. Breakfast and parking.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Are eighteen rooms enough for everyone coming from away?

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: For Lagos, easily. For the cousins from Birmingham, I'm not sure.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: The Birmingham cousins usually stay with Auntie Grace. They told me last week.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Then eighteen is fine. And who's collecting the Lagos guests from the airport? They land on the Friday.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Basically, I was going to sort a van. I just haven't yet.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Tobi.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: I know, I know. I'll book the airport van tomorrow and send everyone the pickup time.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Thank you, my dear. And the rehearsal dinner is the Friday too, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Friday the twentieth. Same evening they land.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Will they be too tired, after such a long flight?

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Lagos people are never too tired for a party.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Mum!

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: She's not wrong.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: Let me see, the jobs that don't have a name yet. The order of service. The photographer timings. The flowers.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: The photographer's booked for six hours. Someone needs to make a shot list.

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Six hours is a lot of photos.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Honestly, I'll do the shot list myself. I know who I want in which photo.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: And the order of service?

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: I used to do the parish newsletter. I could do it, maybe, if someone sends me the words.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Oh, Ingrid, you don't have to.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: I'd like to. It keeps my hands busy.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: The flowers, then. Does anyone know a florist near the church?

turns.speaker: Tobi
turns.text: Sorry, my brother is shouting about the football. One second.

turns.speaker: Joyce
turns.text: I think that's us for today, my dears. Same time next Sunday?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Same time. Love you, Mum. Thank you, everyone.

turns.speaker: Ingrid
turns.text: Goodbye, my dears.
